subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals — dashboards, golden prompts, rollout guardrails
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@fintechco.com>, Amelia Reed <amelia.reed@fintechco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals — dashboards, golden prompts, rollout guardrails

Hi Samir / Amelia,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — appreciate the context on the payments fraud use case and the constraints you have around explainability and auditability. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points you described:
- Limited end-to-end observability for LLM-driven routes (hard to map model outputs back to prompts / user sessions).
- No standardized golden prompt sets or regression evals — QA is manual and ad-hoc, which makes rollouts risky.
- Difficulty tracing production regressions to specific model/version changes (lack of tracing hooks / token-level breadcrumbs).
- Cost surprises in peak windows — need per-route token cost telemetry and guardrails.

Current stack (as you described):
- Production uses hosted LLM endpoints (third-party), a Redis-based cache for prefixes, and internal A/B rollout logic implemented in the application layer.
- Some homegrown evals run nightly for slot-checks but not tied to deployed rollouts.

Success criteria for a PoC / pilot:
1) Per-route observability dashboard showing latency, token cost, error rates, and a diff view for response-quality metrics.
2) Golden prompt ingestion (initial set of ~250 prompts) and automated regression alerts with clear thresholds.
3) Tracing hooks that let you link an inference output back to the originating prompt, user id, and model variant.
4) Rollout guardrails: canary + automatic rollback on quality regression OR manual rollback triggers.
5) Minimal engineering lift for the pilot — we run hosted inference and provide a short integration guide.

Proposed next steps:
- I will share a sample dashboard template + quickstart (Drive link below). See the dashboards folder in the Drive for perf + quality examples.
- Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60–90 min session next week with your ML infra/ops folks; Vivek and Elliot from our side will join to dig into tracing hooks and eval ingestion.
- Please share an initial golden prompt set (CSV) and one representative dataset we can use for baseline metrics.
- We'll scope a 4–6 week pilot: data ingest, dashboard setup, automated evals + basic rollout guardrails.

Attachments: redwood-inference-pricing.pdf (pricing + pilot SOW), discovery-notes-20260304.docx (call notes).
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765

If that looks right, can you confirm who from your infra/ML team should join the deep-dive and whether we need an NDA or additional contracts before we exchange prompts/datasets?

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Wed, Mar 4, 2026 at 9:00 AM, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time this morning — appreciate the context on the payments fraud use case and the constraints you have around explainability and auditability. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.
>
> Pain points you described: ...

Thanks Marissa — this is great and accurately captures our needs. Two quick clarifying Qs before we kick off the deep-dive: 
1) For the automated regression alerts, what metrics do you typically recommend tracking? We care about both quality drift and cost: e.g., accuracy / false positive rate for the fraud detector, KL drift, and token-cost-per-request.
2) For dataset exchange: is the Drive link sufficient or do you recommend a secure S3 bucket (we can generate time-limited creds)?

I can loop in our infra lead (Amelia) on scheduling. We have an internal compliance policy that might require a simple MSA addendum for the pilot — I can surface that once I check with legal. No NDA required at this stage.

Best,
Samir Khan
Head of ML | FintechCo
samir.khan@fintechco.com | +1 (650) 555-4141

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: observability & evals — dashboards, golden prompts, rollout guardrails

Elliot / Vivek — forwarding the external thread. Samir confirmed the recap and asked two quick questions (metrics to track, preferred data exchange).

Internal asks before the deep-dive: 
- Vivek: please prepare an eval/dashboard template showing per-route metrics (latency, token cost, error rate) and a sample quality-diff panel (before/after) for model rollouts.
- Elliot: draft a tracing-hook checklist for instrumentation (required fields, how we surface token-level breadcrumbs, span correlation with user/session IDs).
- Both: propose rollout guardrail defaults for the pilot: e.g., canary at 5% traffic for 48 hrs; alert thresholds: >5% increase in FP rate OR >10% increase in token cost per request triggers auto-rollback.

Deliverables to include in the Drive folder before the deep-dive: dashboard template (Grafana / Redwood Console screenshot), tracing hooks doc (markdown), and an eval ingestion guide (how to upload golden prompt sets and mapping rules).

I'll reply back to Samir with proposed times once Amelia confirms availability. Attaching the pricing/SOW and the discovery notes for context.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Samir — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming no NDA needed at this stage. I'm Vivek (Dir. Solutions Engineering) — I'll run the technical deep-dive from our side.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (60–90 min):
1) Walkthrough of the sample observability dashboard (latency, token cost, error & quality metrics).
2) Tracing hooks & instrumentation: required metadata, sampling strategy, and span correlation.
3) Golden prompt ingestion: file formats, mapping rules, and example evaluation pipeline.
4) Regression alerting and rollout guardrails: thresholds, canary strategy, and auto-rollback mechanics.
5) Q&A and next steps (pilot scoping).

Requests / pre-reads for the meeting:
- A CSV of your initial golden prompts (250 rows is fine) + a small labeled dataset for baseline metrics.
- Access method for exchange: we can accept Drive uploads, or if you prefer S3 signed URLs we can work with that — whichever is easiest on your side.
- Please add the infra/ops engineer who owns production routing to the invite so we can cover rollout instrumentation.

Proposed times (PST): Tue 2026-03-10 10:00–11:30, Wed 2026-03-11 09:00–10:30. Let me know which works.

We'll prepare the dashboard template and tracing checklist ahead of time and drop them in the Drive folder. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
